home.title: Home
home.html:
Hi — I'm Arslan, and I built NATL because I was tired of rewriting the same smoke tests every time the stack changed.

This is a short open-source YAML runner for web UI and API. You write one compact scenario. You run it locally or in CI. When the team swaps Playwright for something else, you change engine: — not the whole suite.

If you're new here: open the guide. Start at Install. Canon can wait until you've seen a green PASS.

Guide

Install, first PASS, then every language block in one page.

Troubleshooting

When it fails, start here before you blame YAML.

Adapters

Playwright by default. Selenium and Cypress when you need them.

Canon

The rules I refuse to break while growing NATL.

Install in one breath

npm install -g @natl/cli @natl/adapter-playwright
npx playwright install chromium
natl --version

Then open the guide.

  • examples/

guide.title: Guide
guide.html:
Guide

I'm Arslan. This is the whole NATL guide in one place — install, first green run, then every public piece of the language, block by block.

Read top to bottom the first time. Later, jump via the contents.

Contents

  1. Install
  2. First run
  3. Scenario anatomy
  4. Project config & env
  5. UI steps
  6. Assert
  7. Extract, set, log, screenshot
  8. Gestures
  9. Vars, secrets, expressions
  10. Page objects
  11. Cases & data
  12. HTTP
  13. Flow
  14. Tags, retries, CLI
  15. Compact form & sugar
  16. What next

Install

You need Node.js 18+ and a terminal.

npm install -g @natl/cli @natl/adapter-playwright
npx playwright install chromium
natl --version

If natl --version prints a number, you're in. If not — Troubleshooting.

Own empty project:

mkdir my-tests && cd my-tests
natl init
natl run tests/

First run

Clone the repo and run the login I keep under examples/ (local HTML fixture — no flaky public site):

git clone https://github.com/arslan-ahmetjanov/natl.git
cd natl/examples
natl run login.yaml

You should see ✓ PASS. Break the assert text on purpose, run again, read the FAIL line, then fix it — that's how you learn the runner.

Scenario anatomy

name: Login smoke
engine: playwright
tags: [smoke]
timeout: 15000
retries: 0
vars:
  base_url: ./fixtures/shop.html
  user: demo@test.com
  pass: secret
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - fill: "#email"
    with: $user
  - fill: "#password"
    with: $pass
  - click: "#login-btn"
  - assert: ".welcome"
    text: "Добро пожаловать"

Root fields I support:

FieldMeaning
nameDisplay name (reports, --grep)
tagsLabels for --tags
engineplaywright | selenium | cypress | http
timeoutDefault step timeout (ms)
retriesExtra full-scenario attempts after failure
varsVariables ($name)
secretsHow to load secrets
importsPage / shared YAML paths
elements / actionsPOM locators and named flows
locator_strategyDefault for string selectors (css | xpath)
casesData-driven rows
dataArray as $data for for:
before_each / after_eachHooks around steps each attempt
stepsMain step list

Per step you may also set timeout, save, debug. To switch engines mid-scenario, use a with: block — that is what the runtime honors.

Project config & env

natl.config.yaml (nearest walking up from the test file):

engine: playwright
browser: chromium
timeout: 15000
base_url: https://staging.example.com
headless: true
viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }
locator_strategy: css
artifacts_dir: artifacts
retries: 0
trace: on-fail
video: off
soft_assert_screenshot: false

Stands without copying URLs into every file:

natl run tests/ --env staging
natl run tests/ --config config/prod.yaml

--env loads config/<name>.yaml. --env and --config are mutually exclusive.

Merge priority: CLI → test YAML → env profile → base config → defaults.

UI steps

VerbForm
gotoURL, file://, or relative path → local file
click / tapSame step; prefer click:
filllocator + sibling with:
selectlocator + with: (option value)
check / unchecklocator
waitms, or selector + visible | hidden | attached | detached
 
- goto: $base_url
- fill: "#email"
  with: $user
- select: "#country"
  with: "KZ"
- check: "#agree"
- click: "#submit"
- wait: 500
- wait: ".modal hidden"

Auto-wait: actions and asserts wait for the target within timeout. You usually do not need wait: ".ok visible" before an assert.

Assert

- assert: ".welcome"
  text: "Hello"              # or is:
- assert: ".welcome"
  contains: "Hell"
- assert: $welcome
  visible: true
- assert: ".banner"
  hidden: true
- assert: ".price"
  attr: class contains "sale"
- assert: current_url == "https://example.com/app"
- assert: current_url contains "/app"
- assert: $ping.status == 200
- assert: ".price"
  text: "$10"
  soft: true
- soft_assert: ".stock"      # alias → soft: true
  visible: true

Attr operators: ==, !=, contains, matches. Soft asserts collect failures and fail at the end; hard assert is fail-fast.

Extract, set, log, screenshot

- get_text: ".title"
  save: title
- get_attr: "a"
  attr: href
  save: href
- set: $total = $price * $qty
- log: "total=$total"
- log: { message: "x", level: warn }   # info|debug|warn|error
- debug: true
- screenshot:
    file: artifacts/shot.png
    full_page: true

Gestures

Same steps for desktop and mobile web — no if: mobile.

- scroll: "#footer"
  into_view: true            # or delta_x / delta_y
- swipe: "#carousel"
  direction: left            # left|right|up|down
  distance: 200
- long_press: "#card"
  duration_ms: 700

Vars, secrets, expressions

SyntaxMeaning
$userVariable
$order.idNested field
$env.KEYEnvironment / .env (missing → error)
$secret.KEYSame store; masked in logs
${ENV:KEY}Legacy compat
 
secrets:
  env:
    file: .env
    encoding: utf-8

vars:
  user: $env.TEST_USER
  pass: $secret.TEST_PASS

Operators: == != > < >= <= contains matches and or not.

Builtins: now, today, random_int, random_string, random_uuid, random_email, len, contains, trim, upper, lower, replace, match, join, map, filter, range.

Runtime also injects current_url for URL checks. See examples/env_login.yaml.

Page objects

# pages/login.yaml
locator_strategy: css
elements:
  email: "#email"
  title:
    strategy: xpath
    value: "//h1"
actions:
  login:
    - fill: $email
      with: $user
    - fill: "#password"
      with: $pass
    - click: "#login-btn"

# scenario
imports:
  - pages/login.yaml
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - do: login.login
    user: $user
    pass: $pass
  - include: login/login
    vars: { user: $user }

do: page.action is the happy path. include: is the lower-level form (file or whole-file reuse). Sibling keys on do: merge into the action scope.

Page files may omit steps. natl run tests/ skips pages/ and config/.

Strategy priority: element object → page locator_strategy → project → css.

Cases & data

cases:
  - { name: user1, user: "a@test.com", pass: secret, expect: "Welcome, A" }
  - { label: user2, user: "b@test.com", pass: secret, expect: "Welcome, B" }
steps:
  - fill: "#email"
    with: $user
  - assert: ".welcome"
    text: $expect

data:
  - { name: one }
  - { name: two }
steps:
  - for: $item in $data
    steps:
      - log: $item.name

Prefer cases: for simple tables; data: + for: for nested / computed loops. Report suffix uses row name / label, else [case N].

HTTP

engine: http
vars:
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8765
steps:
  - get: $base_url/get
    save: ping
  - post: $base_url/post
    headers: { X-Test: "1" }
    body: { hello: world }
    save: echo
  - put: …
  - patch: …
  - delete: …
  - assert: $echo.status == 200
  - assert: $echo.ok == true

Saved shape: { status, headers, body, ok }. Relative URLs resolve against vars.base_url when it is http(s). Legacy api: still works — prefer the verbs.

UI + API in one file:

engine: playwright
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - with: http
    steps:
      - get: $api_base/get
        save: ping
      - assert: $ping.status == 200
  - click: "#refresh"

My HTTP demos need the stub first:

node stubs/echo-server.mjs
natl run http_only.yaml
natl run ui_http_block.yaml

Flow

- if: $role == "admin"
  then:
    - click: "#admin"
  else:
    - click: "#user"

- for: $i in range(1, 5)
  steps:
    - log: $i

- repeat: 3                 # or "3 times" / times: 3
  steps:
    - click: "#next"        # sets $i

- repeat:
    until: $done == true
  steps:
    - click: "#poll"        # max 1000 iterations

- parallel:                 # wait: all (default) | any
  - get: $api/a
    save: a
  - get: $api/b
    save: b

before_each / after_each run around steps on every attempt (including retries).

Tags, retries, CLI

name: Checkout
tags: [smoke, checkout]
retries: 1
natl run tests/ --tags smoke,auth    # OR
natl run tests/ --grep "Login"       # RegExp on name or path
natl run tests/ --retries 2
natl run tests/ --env staging
natl run tests/ --headed
natl run tests/ --engine selenium
natl run tests/ --trace on-fail
natl run tests/ --video off

--tags and --grep combine with AND. Zero matches → exit 1. Retries re-run the whole scenario with a fresh browser context; last attempt wins.

Compact form & sugar

Primary (commit this — valid YAML):

- fill: "#email"
  with: $user
- wait: ".dashboard visible"
- assert: ".welcome"
  text: "Hello"

Runtime sugar (preprocessor; IDEs may flag it):

- fill: "#email" with: $user
- assert: ".welcome" text: "Hello"
- scroll: $footer into_view

IDE autocomplete: wire @natl/core schemas via yaml.schemas — see the CLI README.

What next

  • examples/ — POM, cases, HTTP, gestures, soft assert
  • Troubleshooting — when PASS refuses to show up
  • Adapters — Playwright / Selenium / Cypress / http
  • Canon — the rules I refuse to break

— Arslan

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.html:
Troubleshooting

When something breaks, I look here before I rewrite the scenario.

natl: command not found

npm install -g @natl/cli @natl/adapter-playwright
npm prefix -g
natl --version

Browser / Chromium errors

npx playwright install chromium
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

FAIL … assert / element not found

  • Is the selector still right?
  • Prefer stable #id
  • Check artifacts/

YAML indentation

- fill: "#email"
  with: $user

HTTP examples hang

node stubs/echo-server.mjs
natl run http_only.yaml

Wrong engine

natl engines
npm install -g @natl/adapter-playwright

Still stuck? GitHub issues.

— Arslan

adapters.title: Adapters
adapters.html:
Adapters

The YAML is the contract. Adapters drive a browser — or skip it for HTTP.

enginePackageWhen
playwright@natl/adapter-playwrightDefault
selenium@natl/adapter-seleniumWebDriver / Grid
cypress@natl/adapter-cypressCypress teams (MVP)
httpbuilt into @natl/coreAPI-only
 
natl run suite.yaml --engine selenium

UI + HTTP → with: http in the guide.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.html:
Architecture

  • You write YAML
  • @natl/cli — files, config, filters
  • @natl/core — parse, interpolate, interpret
  • Adapter — Playwright / Selenium / Cypress — or built-in http

Typical flows stay portable when you change engine:. Details live in the canon.

canon.title: Canon
canon.html:
Canon

I believeSo
Short languageA smoke fits on one screen
UI + API togetherwith: http in the same file
Context outside stepsconfig / --env / cases:
Portable via adaptersSame YAML; browsers = adapter capability
Honest ceiling~90% of smokes; escape hatches for the rest
Runner ≠ TMSCLI runs tests — no dashboard product

— Arslan
